transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. Um... well, I guess I'm here because things have been just a little... confusing lately. I hope it's okay to just jump right in? 

As a psychologist myself, I feel a bit embarrassed even saying this, but... I've been having these moments where I hear my friend, Garrett. I hear his voice. And it's... it's as clear as if he’s standing right behind me, like when I'm out on the trail or just sitting in my painting room. And I mean, obviously, the logical part of me knows he’s dead. I know exactly how it sounds. But in the moment, it just feels completely real to me. 

I hope I'm explaining that right... is that the kind of thing you need to know?

Have you experienced any other types of sensory experiences that aren't explained by something actually happening in the environment, such as seeing things, feeling sensations, or smelling things that others don't notice?

Um, no, no other sensory things like that. It's really just... well, just what I mentioned before. I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. It's just... I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. And like I said, it's as clearly as if he’s standing right behind me, whether I'm on the trail or in my painting room. 

I know it sounds crazy, and I promise you, part of me knows he’s dead. I really do. It's just... in the moment, it feels completely real. I'm sorry, I know that's not what you asked, I just... I haven't seen anything or smelled anything weird. Just the voice. Is that... is that helpful? Am I answering your question okay?
Have you ever had any unusual or strange beliefs about these experiences, such as thinking that Garrett is actually trying to communicate with you or that he's sending you special messages?

Oh, no... no, definitely nothing like that. I mean, I know exactly how that would sound, right? With my background, I'm very aware of what it means when people start looking for hidden messages or thinking they're being contacted. So, no, I don't believe he's actually trying to communicate with me from beyond or... or anything supernatural like that. 

It's really just that brief auditory thing I mentioned. I try really hard to keep myself grounded and rational about it when it happens. I really hope I'm not coming across as completely out of touch... I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what's going on so I don't waste your time. Did I explain that okay?
How often do you hear Garrett’s voice, and does it happen even when you’re not thinking about him or feeling emotional?

Um, well... I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is. It's not like it's happening every single hour or anything. Maybe just... a couple of times a week? I try really hard not to let it disrupt my day. 

And... yeah, to answer your other question, it does happen when I'm not even thinking about him or feeling particularly sad. I think that's actually why I finally decided to come in. I could be completely focused on something else, you know, just walking on the trail or mixing paints in my room, feeling totally fine, and then... there it is. 

I know I'm sort of repeating myself, I'm sorry, but it's just exactly like I was saying before. It's his voice, clear as day, like he's standing right behind me. And for that one moment, before my rational brain catches up and reminds me he's dead, it just feels completely, one hundred percent real. I really try to just brush it off when it happens. 

Is... is that a normal kind of grief reaction, maybe? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context and answering what you actually need to know.
Have you ever experienced any other unusual symptoms, such as trouble organizing your thoughts, difficulty expressing yourself, or behaviors that others might find strange or hard to understand?

Um, no, definitely not. I mean... I'm a psychologist, so I'm pretty hyper-aware of how I'm presenting myself to others. I really try to make sure I'm communicating clearly and staying organized. I haven't had anyone tell me I'm acting strange or... or not making sense. 

I'm pretty careful about keeping things professional and put-together, you know? I really wouldn't want to make anyone uncomfortable or come across as disorganized. I just... I hope I'm making sense right now. Am I explaining things clearly enough for you? I really want to make sure I'm giving you a good picture of everything.
Have you ever had any strong beliefs or thoughts about why you’re hearing Garrett’s voice, even if they seemed unusual or hard to explain to others?

Um, no... no, I really don't. Like I said before, I try to stay very rational about the whole thing. I know he's gone. I know grief can do strange things to the brain, especially under stress, so I just... I try to chalk it up to that. A misfiring of the brain, you know? 

I really try not to dwell on it or build any kind of narrative around it because I know how quickly that can spiral into something... well, something unhealthy. I'd never want to let myself go down that path. I just try to acknowledge it happened and move on with my day. 

I hope that's the right way to handle it? I mean, as a professional, that's what I would advise a client to do, just stay grounded in reality... Does that sound like a healthy approach to you? I just want to make sure I'm managing this the best way I can.
Have you ever experienced a period where you heard voices like Garrett's continuously for at least a month, even if it wasn’t every single day?

Um, well... I really wouldn't say it's been continuous, exactly. That makes it sound so... severe. But, um, I guess this whole, um, crisis, if you want to call it that, has been unfolding for about a month now. Ever since Garrett died. 

But like I said, it's just a couple times a week, and I really try to just push past it. I haven't let it get out of hand or anything. It's only been this past month, and I'm really hoping it just fades away on its own as time goes on. 

Is that... does that timeline make sense for someone dealing with a recent loss? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information and not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you ever had any other experiences where you believed something was real that others didn't, or saw or heard things besides Garrett's voice that weren't actually there?

Um, no, absolutely not. I mean, besides the... the thing with Garrett's voice, I haven't had any other experiences like that at all. No other voices, no seeing things, nothing like that. I really pride myself on being very grounded and objective. 

I know how important it is to keep a firm grip on reality, especially in my line of work. I would never let my imagination run away with me or start believing things that aren't true. I'm very careful about that. 

I just... I hope I'm making it clear that the situation with Garrett is very isolated. It's just a grief response, right? That's how it sounds to you, too? I really want to make sure I'm presenting this accurately and not giving the wrong impression.
Have you ever heard any other voices besides Garrett’s, even if just once or twice?

Um, no, definitely not. Just Garrett. And... well, I know I've mentioned it already, but I just want to be really clear about how it happens, so you don't think I'm, you know, completely losing my grip. 

It's just... I'll be out on the trail, or in my painting room, and I'll hear him. And it's so clear. It's exactly as if he's standing right behind me. And I know... I mean, the rational part of my brain knows he's gone, but in that split second, it just feels completely real. 

But it's only him. Never anyone else. I wouldn't want you to think this is some sort of widespread... issue. It's just a very specific, localized reaction to losing him, right? That makes sense for a grieving person to experience, doesn't it? I just want to be sure I'm not making this sound crazier than it is.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others might find strange or impossible, even if you didn’t talk about them or act on them?

Um, no. No, definitely not. I mean, with my background in psychology, I feel like I'd be pretty quick to catch something like that, you know? I'm very, um, grounded in reality. 

I don't have any bizarre theories or... or beliefs that people would find strange or impossible. I just look at things logically. I really try to maintain a very healthy, objective perspective on the world. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure you know that my thought processes are completely intact. It's really just the grief playing tricks on my ears with Garrett, not my actual beliefs about the world changing. That's a reassuring sign, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how stable my thinking actually is.
Have you ever had any fixed beliefs or ideas about the voice or your experience with Garrett that you know are not based in reality, even if you didn't share them with others?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I know what you're asking, like if I thought he was actually haunting me or trying to send me secret messages from the beyond, but... no. It's nothing like that at all. 

I know he's gone. I know the voice is just... it's just my brain misfiring because I miss him so much. I don't have any strange theories about it. I'm a psychologist, so I can recognize that it's just a sensory thing, not a... not a delusion. 

I'm keeping a really good perspective on it, I promise. I know it's not real. That's a good thing, right? The fact that I have that insight means I'm handling it okay, doesn't it? I just really want you to see that I'm staying rational through all of this.
Have you ever experienced any other strange or unreal perceptions, like seeing things that weren't there or believing something strongly that turned out not to be true?

No, definitely not. I mean, like I said, the only thing is... well, I came in because I keep hearing Garrett’s voice. And it's just so vivid. Like I'm out on the trail, or in my painting room, and it's as clearly as if he’s standing right behind me. 

And I want to be super clear—because I don't want you to think I'm completely losing touch with reality—even though a part of me knows he’s dead, in that exact moment, it just feels completely real. But it's only that. I've never seen anything that wasn't there, or believed anything crazy. 

It's just the auditory thing with Garrett. And honestly, given the circumstances, having a sensory memory feel that real... that's a pretty normal grief response, right? I just want to make sure you understand that it's an isolated thing, and I'm not, you know, seeing visions or anything like that. I'm doing okay otherwise, aren't I?
Have you ever had any strong beliefs that turned out not to be true, even if they seemed completely real to you at the time?

No, no, I haven't. I mean, you're asking about, like, delusions, right? With my training, I feel like I'd be the first to spot if I was holding onto a belief that was completely detached from reality. 

I'm really careful to check the facts on things. Even with the grief and... and the stress of everything, I make a point to stay grounded. I don't get swept up in ideas that don't make sense or aren't true. 

It's just the voice, like I mentioned. Nothing else. That's a good sign of my overall stability, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can see I'm really trying to keep a level head about all this.
Have you ever held onto a belief that you later realized wasn’t true, even if it seemed completely real to you at the time?

I think that's... well, that's pretty much what you just asked, isn't it? Unless I'm misunderstanding the question. But no, really, I haven't. 

Like I was saying, I don't get stuck on things that aren't real. I'm very careful about that. I know how important it is to stay objective, especially with my background in psychology. So, no, no false beliefs or anything like that. 

I hope I'm answering these the right way... I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to evaluate me. I am being helpful, right? I really want to make sure we're on the same page and that you can see how hard I'm trying to be completely transparent with you.
Have you ever heard any other voices or sounds that weren't actually there, even if it was just once or in a different situation?

No, definitely not. I mean, I know I've brought it up a few times now, but it's really just Garrett's voice. That's the only reason I even made the appointment. 

It's just... I'll be out on the trail, or in my painting room, and I'll hear him. And it's so clear. It's exactly like he's standing right behind me. And I know I said this before, but I really want to make sure you understand that I'm not completely losing it. Like, part of my brain knows he's gone. But right in that split second, it just feels so incredibly real. 

But it's only him. I've never heard anything else, no other voices, no strange sounds. Nothing like that. I'm pretty sure that's a good sign, right? That it's just this one specific, grief-related thing? I really hope I'm making sense and giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Have you ever had a strong belief that you later realized was completely false, even if it seemed completely real to you at the time?

I... I feel like we might be going in circles a little bit here? I mean, you've asked me about this a couple of times now, and my answer is still the same. No, I haven't had any false beliefs or... or delusions. 

I know it might seem like I'm protesting too much, but I promise I'm being completely honest with you. With my background, I really do try to keep a close eye on my own cognition. I know what to look for, and I just haven't experienced anything like that. 

I'm sorry if I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for... I really am trying to be as helpful as possible. I want to make sure you have everything you need to help me figure out what's going on with Garrett's voice. I'm not being difficult, am I? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

Have you ever had a belief about something in your life that you were absolutely sure was true at the time, but later realized was completely incorrect, even if you didn't act on it or share it with anyone?

I... um, I really don't mean to be frustrating, doctor. I know you have to be thorough, and I completely respect your process. I just... I feel bad because I keep giving you the exact same answer. 

No, I've never had anything like that. No beliefs that turned out to be completely false. I've always prided myself on being pretty grounded, you know? Like I said, as a psychologist, I try to stay very self-aware. I'm always checking my own biases and perceptions. 

I'm really sorry if it seems like I'm just stonewalling you on this. I'm not trying to hide anything, I promise. I just don't have anything to report on that front. I'm still doing okay, right? I mean, I'm being cooperative? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
Have you ever had a moment where you believed something strongly that wasn’t true, even if only for a short time and you didn’t act on it or tell anyone?

Doctor, I... I really don't want to seem difficult or like I'm not listening to you. I know you're asking this in a few different ways, and I appreciate that you're being so careful and thorough with my assessment. I really do. 

But honestly, no. I haven't. Even just for a fleeting moment, I haven't had any sort of break with reality like that, or any bizarre beliefs. I'm really trying to dig deep and think if there's even a minor example I could give you so I'm not just saying 'no' again, but there really isn't. 

I hope you're not getting annoyed with me. I'm really trying to be a good patient here, I promise. It's just... aside from hearing Garrett's voice, my mind feels completely clear and rational. That's okay, right? I'm still giving you the kind of information you need?
Have you ever heard Garrett’s voice in situations that weren’t related to grief or emotional distress, like during routine tasks or when you were feeling calm and distracted?

That's a really good question, doctor. Um... I want to make sure I explain this exactly right for you, so you have what you need. 

No, it wasn't during calm or routine moments. And actually, it wasn't something that happened during my ordinary grief, either. It... well, I feel a little silly admitting this part, because I know I should have been managing my stress better, but it only really started during this specific stretch where I was just... incredibly wired. 

I was barely sleeping at all, and I just felt this intense drive to keep going. I was taking on these completely impossible projects, just working around the clock. I had never heard him like that before that... that shift in my mood. It was only during that really driven, sleepless phase. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm being clear enough. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context so you can figure this out. I'm doing okay, right?
